statusDefinitions.methodImplemented: A public client method exists for this operation.
statusDefinitions.typeCoverage: complete means common request and response options have dedicated exported types; partial means a generic record or escape hatch remains.
statusDefinitions.unitTests: present means at least one unit test covers the method or shared transport path; it does not mean every action is covered.
statusDefinitions.integrationTests: tested means the exact operation behavior has passed an integration test on every pinned Solr version listed as tested; partial means some versions or behavior are tested; not-run means no real Solr server test has been executed for the operation.

entries.notes: Document add is exercised in the CRUD smoke test on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Named SolrUpdateOptions now expose overwrite, commitWithin, and SolrCloud _route_ serialization; request parameter serialization and invalid values are covered by unit tests. Runtime verification of route/commitWithin options remains unverified on Solr 8/9/10. Field-specific SolrAtomicUpdateOperation and SolrAtomicUpdateDocument types plus atomicUpdate() support set, add, add-distinct, remove, removeregex, and numeric inc. Unit, consumer type, and pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0 integration tests cover atomic updates. Single JSON documents use /update/json/docs; arrays use /update. Both forms are integration-tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. commitWithin is a scheduling hint whose hard/soft behavior is controlled by Solr's commitWithin configuration; the client does not force either commit type. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Unit tests assert the single-document, document-array, and command-map JSON endpoint selection, typed response header, and HTTP error propagation. Unit tests assert single-document, document-array, and command-map endpoint selection, typed response headers, and HTTP error propagation.
Field-specific atomic update modifiers are covered by unit/type assertions and integration tests on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0.

SolrCloud CREATE/LIST/DELETE, alias lifecycle, implicit-router shard lifecycle, named ADDREPLICA/DELETEREPLICA lifecycle, replica property add/delete and BALANCESHARDUNIQUE responses, plus multi-node MOVEREPLICA and REBALANCELEADERS leader reassignment are tested on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images (CI #177, #192, #209, and PR #142 CI #224). MOVEREPLICA verifies the named replica becomes active on a different live node. REBALANCELEADERS assigns preferredLeader to an active non-leader and verifies it becomes shard leader. Snapshot, backup, and cluster-state response models remain unverified. Additional operation evidence: Typed SolrCloud collection backup/restore actions and asynchronous REQUESTSTATUS/DELETESTATUS tracking. Full backup, list, restore, query read-back, and delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 with a shared local filesystem volume mounted on both SolrCloud nodes. S3 and other external repositories are not certified.

SolrCommitOptions expose waitSearcher, softCommit, expungeDeletes (hard-commit only), and openSearcher (request parameter); integration tests cover openSearcher=false and expungeDeletes on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0. Legacy CommitOptions.maxSegments is deprecated and rejected. Update methods default to SolrUpdateResponse; successful output validation is wired to the public operation key. SolrHttpError.errorResponse exposes SolrErrorResponse while solrError remains the normalized detail. Mock validation tests cover success/error paths; add/update responseHeader.status is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4/9.11.0/10.1.0.

Config API set-user-property plus GET /config/overlay userProps read-back pass on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup unsets the property (CI #166). Live Security API authentication and authorization checks pass in the dedicated security matrix (CI #162). Common set-property/unset-property names and property-specific values are exported for the shared Solr 8.11/9.11/10.1 baseline; typed command, effective-config, and config-overlay response models are exported. Version-specific common properties remain outside the cross-version property union. TypeScript consumer fixtures cover the shared documented set-property allow-list with value-specific types, unset-property names, arbitrary user properties, and typed effective-config/overlay/command response models; these are compile-time guarantees, not additional live-server assertions.
CoreAdmin CREATE, STATUS, and RELOAD pass with unique disposable cores on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; fixture cleanup UNLOADs them (CI #145).

Typed SolrExportParams requires fl and sort, supports filter query arrays, raw or structured sort expressions, batchSize, response writer selection, optional local expr, and customParams. export() returns the raw backpressure-aware Response; exportStream() exposes the byte body. Sort fields must be single-valued docValues int/long/float/double/string fields; fl additionally supports date/boolean and multi-valued fields. includeStoredFields is documented for Solr 10.1 but remains version-specific. Existing live raw-response integration test covers Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0; new unit tests cover typed serialization and streamed chunk consumption.
Reads the effective configuration through GET /config. The method has dedicated request serialization and integration evidence.
Reads the persisted Config API overlay through GET /config/overlay. Kept separate from getConfig because the endpoint and semantics differ.
JVM Metrics API response passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. Solr 8/9 return the classic JSON registry; Solr 10.1 returns Prometheus exposition text.

Optimize followed by query asserting committed documents remain available passed on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments and waitSearcher with unit and consumer type coverage; the existing optimize behavior remains integration-tested on all pinned versions. SolrOptimizeOptions expose maxSegments, waitSearcher, and openSearcher; maxSegments is optimize-only and defaults to Solr's unlimited target. The integration test exercises maxSegments on all pinned versions. openSearcher is request-parameter serialized; its optimize-specific runtime effect remains unverified. Generic SolrResponse<TDocument> and SolrQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> types expose document metadata, classic facet counts, caller-shaped JSON facets, highlighting, grouping, stats, and debug sections. Consumer compile tests verify document inference and response-section property types. Basic query serialization and document retrieval plus cursorMark multi-page traversal are tested on the pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 images; typed declarations do not certify every optional response section at runtime. Typed classic Facet Component options cover field facets and per-field limit/offset/sort/mincount/missing/prefix/method overrides, query facets, and numeric/date range facets with include/other/hardend and filter/dv methods. Solr date bucketing uses range facets; legacy facet.date parameters were removed in Solr 6. Integration coverage asserts field/query counts and numeric/date range response sections on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed highlighting options cover field selection, highlighter method, snippet/fragment sizing, field matching, alternate fields, phrase and multi-term highlighting, encoders/tags, and per-field overrides. Unit and consumer type tests cover parameter serialization and invalid values; integration tests verify returned snippets on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed Result Grouping options cover group.field, group.func, group.query, per-group limit/offset/sort, group format/main/ngroups/truncate/facet/cache settings; typed grouped response models expose matches, group counts, and per-group document lists. Typed collapse and expand options serialize the Collapsing Query Parser filter and Expand component parameters, with expanded document maps in the response. Standalone integration tests verify field grouping, group sorting, collapse selection, and expansion on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Function grouping and collapse remain subject to Solr's documented distributed/shard-local limitations. Typed Stats Component options support repeated fields, per-field local statistic selection, percentiles, cardinality, tag/key/excludeTags, global stats facets, and calcDistinct. SolrFieldStats response models include nested facet breakdowns, percentiles, and cardinality. Unit and consumer type tests cover encoding and response properties; integration tests verify numeric aggregates, distinct values/counts, cardinality, and category breakdowns on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Typed MoreLikeThis Search Component options cover field selection, result count, term/document-frequency thresholds, word/token/query-term limits, boosting, query fields, and interesting terms. Unit and consumer type tests cover serialization and response typing; integration tests verify similar-document results on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Geospatial geofilt/bbox filter and geodist helper serialization is covered by unit/consumer type tests, but these helpers have no live Solr integration test and remain runtime-unverified on all three pinned versions.

JSON Request API query body now has a typed SolrJsonQueryRequest model and recursive JSON Facet API terms/query/range definitions, nested metrics, and domain transformations. SolrJsonQueryResponse<TDocument, TJsonFacet> exposes caller-typed facet results. Unit and consumer type tests cover nested serialization and invalid discriminators; integration tests verify terms/query/range facets, nested metrics, and excludeTags domain behavior on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Other JSON Request API options remain available through params or the legacy custom-body overload.

Typed V1 ReplicationHandler commands for enablereplication, disablereplication, indexversion, fetchindex, abortfetch, snappull, abort, enablepoll, disablepoll, details, filelist, backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup; replicationFile() returns raw filecontent streams. Live integration coverage on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0 covers indexversion, details, filelist, and filecontent. enablereplication/disablereplication are integration-tested on a configured leader; fetchindex/abortfetch (Solr 10), snappull/abort (Solr 8/9), enablepoll, and disablepoll have unit serialization coverage, but a multi-core leader/follower fetch cycle is not yet certified. Core-level backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are integration-tested on all three pinned versions. Filelist uses the generation returned by newer Solr indexversion responses and falls back to the legacy indexversion parameter when that field is absent. Additional operation evidence: Core-level ReplicationHandler backup, restore, restorestatus, and deletebackup are typed. Backup defaults to the core dataDir; restore status is polled with restorestatus. Full backup/restore/read-back/delete cycle is integration-tested on Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Custom filesystem locations must be permitted by server allowPaths.
Returns raw replication file content as a Response stream; distinct from command-based replication operations.

Field, field-type, dynamic-field add/replace/delete and copy-field add/delete commands are unit-tested for exact serialization and integration-tested with responseHeader.status plus schema read-back on pinned Solr 8.11.4, 9.11.0, and 10.1.0. Integration tests verify full schema metadata, name, version, uniqueKey, and similarity response envelopes on all pinned versions. Similarity plugin mutation remains runtime-unverified. The public client implements V1 Schema API routes; Solr 10 V2 routes are not included.
